steps.label: Boundary stiffness for the Two-Way Akinci force, same regime as 51_couple_rigid_fluid_twoway.json (WCSPHFluid::estimatePressureCoe(0.6, 98.0) = 58.8)
Shallow pool just below ScenePreset::SphereDrop's fixed y=3/r=0.5 spawn (bottom of the sphere starts at y=2.5, clear of the pool's y=2.2 top)
Domain floor at y=0; x/z open
Baseline run: One-Way (SDF penalty only, no reaction force back on the sphere)
Sphere falls into the pool, unaffected by any buoyant reaction (~0.4s)
Comparison run: Two-Way (Akinci boundary particles, buoyant reaction now applies)
Two-Way confirmed active for this dynamic, non-Plane body
Sphere falls into the pool, same duration, now with a buoyant reaction pushing back (~0.4s)
Change: Two-Way sphere height after falling
Invariant: the Two-Way run's fluid stays bounded -- it used to explode to max particle Y in the thousands on sphere impact (docs/issue/CODEBASE_ISSUES.md 1.6)
Invariant: the sphere is still falling, but slower than the discrete free-fall velocity -g*dt*n = -3.92 the One-Way run reproduces exactly
